OncallBot: :rotating_light: P1 Pager: production - encoder-service Canary cutover caused widespread CrashLoopBackOffs across inference pods. Auto-escalation to on-call @Sam. Logs: https://internal.logs/relevant-link
Sam: On it, grabbing context. Which rollout triggered this?
Alice: Canary cutover started ~15m ago, feature flag ffd_encoder_v2 rolled to 20% via launchpad. Saw some init containers failing during startup.
Mike: Looking at k8s: many pods in CrashLoopBackOff, init container `fetch-model` failing with `exit code 137` on node drain notices. HPA triggered scale due to probe flapping.
Carla: CS: customers reporting elevated 503s and increased latency for realtime endpoints. No billing impact yet but user-facing errors. Ticket numbers popping up.
Sam: Ok kill the feature flag to stop new traffic to canary. Alice, can you toggle the kill-switch?
Alice: Toggling now: `./launchpad toggle-flag ffd_encoder_v2 off --env prod`
Alice: :white_check_mark: flag off. Routing should stop sending new canary traffic.
Mike: Running `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=encoder` shows pods still restarting. Root cause looks like combination of init fetch failures (OOM / eviction) + HPA misconfig that multiplied pods during drain.
Mike: Snippet of failing init logs:
```
2026-06-12T09:12:01Z fetch-model: downloading weights
2026-06-12T09:12:03Z fetch-model: write failed: ENOSPC
2026-06-12T09:12:04Z kernel: Killed process 12345 (fetch-model) total-vm:2048000kB
```
Sam: ENOSPC? but nodes had disk pressure + kubelet evicting init containers. Why did drain start?
Alice: There was an automated node drain for stacked upgrades in eu-west-1 at the same time. Node drain controller kicked off due to alert `node.disk.pressure` on 3 nodes.
Carla: So two simultaneous events: canary traffic + scheduled maintenance drain. Customer impact correlates with those windows. Noting top customers affected and sending interim message.
Sam: Mitigation plan: 1) Keep kill-switch off 2) Pause any automated drains in eu-west-1 3) Scale down HPA temp to minReplicas=2 4) Evict stuck pods and restart with `imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent` fallback.
Mike: Executing step 2 & 3: `kubectl annotate node <node> maintenance=true` and `kubectl patch hpa encoder -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'`
Mike: Also pushing a hotfix to init container to gracefully handle partial downloads and avoid ENOSPC crash. Building image `encoder-init:vhot-20260612`.
Alice: Rolling a rollback of the canary workloads to previous replicaSets for encoder: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/encoder --to-revision=42 -n prod`
OncallBot: Escalation note: SOC and SRE teams paged. Recording timeline, will create postmortem ticket INC-20260612-01.
Carla: CS update sent: "We're investigating degraded behavior in inference endpoints after a deployment. We have paused the rollout, and a rollback is in progress. We'll provide an ETA in 30m."
Sam: Observability: tailing `/metrics` shows request error-rate dropping since flag off and rollback started. Monitoring for stability for 15m before full close.
Mike: After rollback and HPA tweak, pod restarts decreased. Logs show init container succeeding on nodes not under disk pressure.
Alice: Confirming traffic is back to stable baseline for most routes, some customers still affected due to in-flight requests during the drain.
Carla: CS: updating impacted customer list and offering targeted retries for queued jobs.
Sam: Passing to next oncall for daytime: @Alice will own follow-up remediation and postmortem writeup.
Alice: Accepted handoff. TODOs: capture exact sequence for drain + rollout overlap, add guard to block canary cutovers during cluster maintenance, add ENOSPC handling in init.
OncallBot: Incident state -> mitigated. P1 -> monitoring. Postmortem: INC-20260612-01 assigned to Alice, due 2026-06-19.
Carla: Great work team. Thanks :pray:
